space/pairs: The web is full of images with text written beside them. CLIP trains on such pairs: a photo, and its caption.
space/encoders: It has two encoders. An image encoder turns each photo into a vector. A text encoder, starting from the embeddings of the caption's tokens, turns each caption into a vector of the same width, d. Both are scaled to length one.
space/sim: Stack a batch of N images, and their N captions. One matrix product gives every image's dot product with every caption: an N by N grid of similarities.
diagonal/diag: Pair i is image i with the caption written for it, so the right pairs sit on the diagonal.
diagonal/rows: Each row is a contrastive problem: a softmax over the captions, and a cross-entropy that wants image i to pick caption i. The other N minus one captions in the row are its negatives: here, two.
diagonal/cols: The columns get the same treatment: each caption should pick its own image. The loss averages the two directions.
diagonal/count: With three pairs, the grid holds nine similarities. Training pushes the three on the diagonal up, and the six negatives down.
zeroshot/names: After training, CLIP can sort images into classes it was never trained on. Write one caption per class: a photo of a tree, a photo of a boat, a photo of a sunset.
zeroshot/embed: Embed the captions with the text encoder, and the image with the image encoder.
zeroshot/pick: Score the image against each caption by the dot product: zero point three one, zero point one two, and zero point zero five. The highest wins: tree. No labeled tree images were needed. The classifier was written in words.
